name: Parathyroidectomy
portPlacementOrIncision: Focused lateral approach or standard collar incision

pimpingQuestions.question: The superior and inferior parathyroid glands derive from which pharyngeal pouches, and which has more variable position?
pimpingQuestions.answer: Superior: 4th pharyngeal pouch (dorsal wing, consistent position behind upper thyroid). Inferior: 3rd pharyngeal pouch (descend with thymus, longer migration = more variable position — from angle of mandible to anterior mediastinum).

pimpingQuestions.question: What percentage of patients have ectopic parathyroid glands, and what are the common locations?
pimpingQuestions.answer: 15-20% have ectopic glands. Common locations: intrathyroidal (3-5%), carotid sheath, tracheoesophageal groove, thymus (most common ectopic site for inferior glands), mediastinum (may require sternotomy or VATS), and retroesophageal. Preoperative sestamibi scan and 4D-CT help localize.

pimpingQuestions.question: What is the blood supply to the parathyroid glands, and what is the consequence of devascularization?
pimpingQuestions.answer: Primarily the inferior thyroid artery (supplies both superior and inferior glands in 80%). The superior thyroid artery contributes to the superior glands. Each gland has a single end-artery — devascularization causes infarction and hypoparathyroidism. If devascularized, mince the gland into 1mm pieces and autotransplant into the sternocleidomastoid or forearm muscle.

pimpingQuestions.question: What is the intraoperative PTH protocol (Miami criteria), and when do you consider the operation successful?
pimpingQuestions.answer: Baseline PTH drawn before incision. After adenoma excision, PTH levels at 5 and 10 minutes. Success: PTH drops >50% from the highest pre-excision value AND falls into the normal range. If PTH doesn't drop adequately, search for multigland disease, ectopic gland, or supernumerary (5th) gland.

pimpingQuestions.question: What is the difference between primary, secondary, and tertiary hyperparathyroidism surgically?
pimpingQuestions.answer: Primary: single adenoma (85%) — focused parathyroidectomy. Secondary: all four glands hyperplastic from chronic kidney disease — subtotal (3.5-gland) parathyroidectomy or total with autotransplant. Tertiary: autonomous PTH secretion after renal transplant (previously secondary) — subtotal parathyroidectomy if hypercalcemia persists >1 year post-transplant.
